newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus police press charges over deadly dogfights.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus police press charges over deadly dogfights.

text.p: Four Greek Cypriots were charged on Wednesday with organising vicious dogfights for betting purposes and released on bail, police said.
The suspects, charged under the animal welfare law, were accused of organising deadly dogfights in the southeastern district of Famagusta between January 1995 and March 1997.

They are to reappear in court in a week to answer the charges, which carry a maximum jail term of six months, a 500-pound ($980) fine or both, for first-time offenders. The penalties are doubled for repeat offenders.

Footage of one fight, apparently shot by an organiser to verify the victory by a tiny pit bull terrier over an Alsatian, was shown on local television last week, prompting a storm of protest from animal welfare groups.
